This edition has no WebView and no JavaScript engine. Your input is processed by a Kotlin port of the level\'s PHP; the resulting HTML is then analysed natively. If a real browser would have executed script (<script>, on*= event handlers, javascript: URLs, CSP-allowed sources, JSONP callbacks), the app shows ⚠ XSS fired with a simulated effect (alert/prompt/confirm text in a native dialog, document.cookie value, redirects/exfiltration described but never sent). Safe levels show the escaped output and blocked.
\u0020DOM XSS: type the full URL; the part after # is never sent to the \'server\' but is still read by the simulated document.write().
\u0020Guestbook entries are stored in the bundled SQLite database.
\u0020CSP rules (allowed hosts, nonce, \'self\', JSONP callback) are evaluated natively. Nothing is fetched: for allowed external URLs you supply the simulated file content.
\u0020The page\'s client-side token functions (md5(rot13), reverse, sha256 chain) are re-implemented in Kotlin; use the \'Run in console\' helpers or tamper the hidden token field.
Commands run in a simulated shell over a fake Debian file system; no real device command is ever executed.
Files are saved to the app\'s private directory. Uploaded .php files can be \'requested\' through a tiny PHP/webshell simulator backed by the fake shell.
Included files come from a bundled fake web root, a fake Debian FS and this app\'s own sandbox (/data/data/org.dvwa.android/…). Remote URLs are never fetched.
Google reCAPTCHA is replaced with a locally drawn text CAPTCHA. Hidden fields and headers can be edited in the tamper panel.
Redirects to external sites are shown, never followed (no INTERNET permission).
DVWA is a deliberately vulnerable practice app. Everything runs offline inside this app: no internet, no WebView. Practise only here or on systems you own or are allowed to test.
Log in with admin / password. Open the menu (☰) and choose DVWA Security to switch between Low, Medium, High and Impossible. Start with Low.
Pick a module like SQL Injection or XSS from the menu. Type a payload, press Submit and watch the result. Use View Source to read the PHP code and View Help for hints.
The orange Intercept & tamper panel lets you edit hidden fields, headers and cookies. Go to URL… opens pages directly. The User Guide in the menu explains every module step by step.

Welcome to Damn Vulnerable Web Application!

Damn Vulnerable Web Application (DVWA) is a PHP/MySQL web application that is damn vulnerable. Its main goal is to be an aid for security professionals to test their skills and tools in a legal environment, help web developers better understand the processes of securing web applications and to aid both students & teachers to learn about web application security in a controlled class room environment.
The aim of DVWA is to practice some of the most common web vulnerabilities, with various levels of difficulty, with a simple straightforward interface.

It is up to the user how they approach DVWA. Either by working through every module at a fixed level, or selecting any module and working up to reach the highest level they can before moving onto the next one. There is not a fixed object to complete a module; however users should feel that they have successfully exploited the system as best as they possible could by using that particular vulnerability.
Please note, there are both documented and undocumented vulnerabilities with this software. This is intentional. You are encouraged to try and discover as many issues as possible.
Every module has View Source (the real DVWA PHP for the current level), Compare All and View Help buttons.

Everything is native Android UI and runs offline inside the app: no WebView, no embedded web server, no INTERNET permission. A bundled SQLite database, a simulated Debian file system/shell and a PHP-behaviour port in Kotlin stand in for the LAMP stack. All vulnerabilities only touch this app\'s own sandboxed data.
Damn Vulnerable Web Application is damn vulnerable! Only practise on systems you own or are authorised to test.

1. Setup / Reset DB restores the 5 users and the guestbook (it is also created on first launch).
2. Log in with admin / password. Other accounts: gordonb / abc123, 1337 / charley, pablo / letmein, smithy / password.
3. Pick a level in DVWA Security (Low, Medium, High, Impossible).
4. Choose a module from the menu. Use View Source and View Help on each screen.
How web concepts map to this app

• Hidden form fields, headers (Referer, User-Agent), cookies and client-side limits (maxlength, dropdowns) are editable in each module\'s orange \"Intercept & tamper\" panel — the native equivalent of Burp Suite / DevTools.\n• The toolbar menu has a simulated address bar (Go to URL…) to request pages directly, e.g. /vulnerabilities/authbypass/.\n• Request timing is shown for blind/time-based attacks.

• Database: real bundled SQLite. Vulnerable levels build SQL by string concatenation; Impossible uses prepared statements. MySQL-isms are translated: # comments, user(), database(), version()/@@version, concat(), substring()/mid(), ascii(), sleep(n) and an information_schema.tables/columns/schemata emulation. sqlite_master works too.\n

• Command Injection: a fake shell interpreter (; && || | & $( ) and backticks; ping, id, whoami, uname, ls, cat, head, tail, grep, wc, find, ps, env, echo …) over a fake Debian file system. No real device command is ever run.\n

• XSS (DOM/Reflected/Stored), CSP Bypass and JavaScript Attacks: there is no browser. The HTML the vulnerable PHP would have produced is analysed natively; when a browser would have executed script you get “⚠ XSS fired” plus a simulated alert dialog. Safe levels show escaped output.\n
• File Upload / File Inclusion use the app\'s private storage; uploaded .php files run through a small webshell simulator.\n
• Insecure CAPTCHA uses a local text CAPTCHA instead of Google reCAPTCHA.\n
• Nothing ever leaves the device; external redirects/requests are displayed, not performed.
Damn Vulnerable Web Application (DVWA) is a PHP/MySQL web application that is damn vulnerable.

This app (v2.1.0) is an offline, fully native Android (Kotlin) re-implementation of DVWA\'s modules for personal practice. The original DVWA is by Ryan Dewhurst (ethicalhack3r), Robin Wood (digininja) and contributors, released under the GNU General Public License v3; its help texts, images and PHP sources (shown via View Source) are bundled under that licence.

You can set the security level to low, medium, high or impossible. The security level changes the vulnerability level of DVWA:\n\n

1. Low - This security level is completely vulnerable and has no security measures at all. It\'s use is to be as an example of how web application vulnerabilities manifest through bad coding practices and to serve as a platform to teach or learn basic exploitation techniques.\n

2. Medium - This setting is mainly to give an example to the user of bad security practices, where the developer has tried but failed to secure an application. It also acts as a challenge to users to refine their exploitation techniques.\n

3. High - This option is an extension to the medium difficulty, with a mixture of harder or alternative bad practices to attempt to secure the code. The vulnerability may not allow the same extent of the exploitation, similar in various Capture The Flags (CTFs) competitions.\n
4. Impossible - This level should be secure against all vulnerabilities. It is used to compare the vulnerable source code to the secure source code.
